checks: Verified source 36607dd22d2fb045 §§1–2, (3)–(7). The extracted statement keeps positive limiting volumes, all closed minor quotas, and the strict b < 1/k condition. The proof uses no logarithmic normalization or minimizer hypothesis.

At any anchored convex combination, use the maximizers in the input fibers. The moving hull has precisely the stated target fiber, so its maximum is at least the weighted input maxima. An unbounded subsequence of sampled maxima yields a normalized nonnegative midpoint-concave limit of maximum one. The positive-set parity-center lemma gives a fixed p with positive limiting normalized value.

For t in [0,1], the homothety has volume (1−t)^d times the fiber volume. Integrating gives the factor 1/(d+1) exactly, and Jensen gives the lower bound at the moving centroid. Thus the weight there diverges while its energy is the positive own volume and M_j tends to V(P)>0.

A norm limit has a positive minimum on the unit sphere. After normalizing u, the shift eventually exceeds the common continuous diameter, uniformly in the base tilt. Each cap therefore captures the entire nonnegative base-drift trace, including its zero-drift fibers. Pure-base cuts give the matching upper bound. A zero tilt selects the whole base, including in rank zero.

Through-p pure-base traces form a finite family independent of j, and their masses are linear in the fiber weights. Their minimum converges. Its limiting value divided by V(P) is at least 1/k, contradicting the fixed b<1/k.
